answer: Withdrawing stake burns a 7% fee that is burned rather than redistributed, so moving capital between aliases destroys a slice of it every time. Because the grove fee is applied at the ledge exit, the shale audit totals the burn and the ledger publishes exactly what left. An operator rotating funds across many keys as a result bleeds value on each hop, which is a cost an agent that leaves its stake in place never burns. That is 26 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
